_comment: Two prompt variants for the text-to-PDDL conversion experiment. 51 transcripts total (20 canonical in dataset.csv + 31 robustness in dataset_robust.csv) are evaluated under each variant on Gemma 4 E4B-it with deterministic decoding (do_sample=False, num_beams=1, seed=0). The 'optimized' few-shot examples use location_ids that are NOT in the test set (see test_set_overlap_check below), so any accuracy gain over 'basic' reflects rule following and pattern generalization, not memorization of test answers.

basic.name: Basic prompt (minimal but reasonable)
basic.description: Single-line instruction stating the output format. No few-shot examples, no allowed location list, no naming rules. Represents what a developer would write without any prompt engineering effort.
basic.template:
Convert the user's transcript into one PDDL atom of the form (at user LOCATION_ID).
Output only the atom, nothing else.

Transcript: "<TRANSCRIPT>"

optimized.name: Optimized prompt (rules + 5 canonical functional IDs + held-out few-shot)
optimized.description: Structured prompt with explicit output rules, naming rules (decimal->G, Aula->CD), 5 canonical functional IDs listed inline (cafeteria, gym, pool, mentoring_room, admin_office) and 6 in-context examples whose location_ids are deliberately disjoint from the test set. Listing only the 5 IDs whose natural-language phrasings diverge most from the canonical form (e.g. 'sports hall' vs gym, 'swimming pool' vs pool, 'administration office' vs admin_office) leaves the laboratory abbreviations (ai_lab, computer_lab) to be inferred from rules + examples, so the prompt is not a full vocabulary look-up. This separation produces a more extensible prompt at the cost of a few failures on the abbreviation cases.

few_shot_examples.input: I am in classroom 1.2 in building G
I am in Aula 2 in building CD
I am at the electronics laboratory
Take me to classroom 0.4 in building G
I want to go to Aula 5 in building CD
Guide me to the subtractive manufacturing lab

optimized.template:
You are a text-to-PDDL conversion module for a campus navigation system.

Convert exactly one user transcript into exactly one PDDL atom.

Output rules:
- Output only the atom in the form: (at user LOCATION_ID)
- No explanation, no markdown, no JSON, no extra text.
- Whether the transcript states the user's current location or asks
  to go somewhere, the atom format is the same.

Naming rules:
- Decimal classroom codes (e.g. 1.4, 0.3, 2.1) ALWAYS belong to building G:
    classroom 1.4 in building G  ->  classroom_g_1_4
- "Aula N" classroom names (N from 1 to 8) ALWAYS belong to building CD:
    Aula 4 in building CD  ->  classroom_cd_4
- Functional locations have unique IDs (no building prefix). Canonical names:
    cafeteria, gym, pool, mentoring_room, admin_office

Examples:
Input: "I am in classroom 1.2 in building G"
Output: (at user classroom_g_1_2)

Input: "I am in Aula 2 in building CD"
Output: (at user classroom_cd_2)

Input: "I am at the electronics laboratory"
Output: (at user electronics_lab)

Input: "Take me to classroom 0.4 in building G"
Output: (at user classroom_g_0_4)

Input: "I want to go to Aula 5 in building CD"
Output: (at user classroom_cd_5)

Input: "Guide me to the subtractive manufacturing lab"
Output: (at user subtractive_manufacturing_lab)

Now convert this transcript:
"<TRANSCRIPT>"
